items.followUp: Describe the role of light reactions in photosynthesis and name their main products.

rubric.why: Dark reactions do not directly require light, occur in the stroma and use ATP and NADPH from the light reactions.
rubric.description: Defines the dark reactions and identifies their location and energy sources.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the reactions as light-independent, occurring in the stroma and using ATP and NADPH.

rubric.why: Carbon fixation begins when carbon dioxide combines with RuBP and produces 3-PGA.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that carbon dioxide combines with RuBP to form 3-PGA.

rubric.why: ATP and NADPH are used to reduce 3-PGA to G3P, also called PGAL.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that ATP and NADPH convert 3-PGA into G3P or PGAL.

rubric.why: Some G3P or PGAL is used to form glucose and other carbohydrates.
rubric.description: States the fate of some G3P or PGAL.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that G3P or PGAL is used to form glucose or carbohydrates.

rubric.why: The remaining G3P or PGAL is used to regenerate RuBP, which allows the cycle to continue.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that remaining G3P or PGAL is used to regenerate RuBP.

modelAnswer: Dark reactions, also called the Calvin cycle, are light-independent reactions of photosynthesis that occur in the stroma and use ATP and NADPH from the light reactions.
Carbon fixation: carbon dioxide combines with RuBP to form an unstable six-carbon compound, which splits into 3-PGA molecules.
Reduction: ATP and NADPH are used to convert 3-PGA into G3P (also called PGAL).
Some G3P is used to form glucose and other carbohydrates.
The remaining G3P is used, with energy from ATP, to regenerate RuBP.

items.followUp: Define hypertension and describe one cause and one possible effect.

rubric.why: Cardiovascular disorders affect the heart and blood vessels.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying disorders or diseases of the heart and blood vessels.

rubric.why: A myocardial infarction commonly occurs when a coronary artery is blocked.
rubric.description: Identifies the immediate cause of myocardial infarction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a coronary artery becomes blocked.

rubric.why: The blockage reduces the supply of oxygenated blood to part of the heart muscle.
rubric.description: Explains the effect of the blockage on the heart muscle's oxygen supply.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the blockage reduces oxygenated blood reaching the heart muscle.

rubric.why: Reduced oxygen supply causes heart muscle cells to become damaged or die.
rubric.description: States the resulting damage to the heart muscle.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that heart muscle cells are damaged or die.

rubric.why: Chest pain, sometimes spreading to the arm, and symptoms such as sweating or nausea can occur during a myocardial infarction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for severe chest pain together with another valid symptom, such as sweating, nausea or pain spreading to the arm.

modelAnswer: Cardiovascular disorders are diseases or abnormalities of the heart and blood vessels.
Myocardial infarction, or a heart attack, occurs when a coronary artery becomes blocked, commonly by a blood clot forming over a fatty deposit.
The blockage reduces the supply of oxygenated blood to part of the heart muscle, causing its cells to become damaged or die.
A person may experience severe chest pain, which can spread to the arm, as well as sweating or nausea.
Myocardial infarction is a medical emergency.

items.followUp: Define an organ and give one example.

rubric.why: A tissue consists of similar cells working together to perform a particular function.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing tissue as similar cells working together to perform a function.

rubric.why: Xylem is a valid example of a tissue.
rubric.description: Gives an example of a tissue.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid example of a tissue.

modelAnswer: A tissue is a group of similar cells that work together to perform a particular function.
Xylem is an example of a tissue.
